```{r, eval=FALSE}
data%>%
  group_by(diagnosiscat)%>%
  count()


my_skim <- skim_with(base = sfl(n = length))

agebl.sum<-data%>%
  group_by(diagnosiscat)%>%
  dplyr::select(agebl)%>%
  my_skim()%>%
  transmute(Variable=skim_variable,Group=diagnosiscat,n=n,Mean=numeric.mean,SD=numeric.sd,Min=numeric.p0,Median=numeric.p50,Max=numeric.p100,IQR=numeric.p75-numeric.p25)


sex.sum<-data%>%
  group_by(diagnosiscat,sex)%>%
  dplyr::summarise(n=n())%>%
  mutate(percentage=paste0(round(100*n/sum(n),2),'%'))



my_skim <- skim_with(base = sfl(n = length))

packyears.sum<-data%>%
  group_by(diagnosiscat)%>%
  dplyr::select(packyears)%>%
  my_skim()%>%
    transmute(Variable=skim_variable,Group=diagnosiscat,Mean=numeric.mean,SD=numeric.sd,Median=numeric.p50,Max=numeric.p100,Q75=numeric.p75,Q25=numeric.p25)



data$eversmok.yn<-ifelse(eversmok==0,"no","yes")

eversmok<-data%>%
  group_by(diagnosiscat,eversmok.yn)%>%
  dplyr::summarise(n=n())%>%
  mutate(percentage=paste0(round(100*n/sum(n),1),'%'))%>%
  transmute(eversmok= eversmok.yn, n=n,percentage=percentage)
  


livesalone.sum<-data%>%
  group_by(diagnosiscat,livesalone)%>%
  dplyr::summarise(n=n())%>%
  mutate(percentage=paste0(round(100*n/sum(n),1),'%'))
```

```{r eval=FALSE}

data$mmsecat<-cut(data$mmsebltotal,c(0,23,27,30),labels = c("<24","24-27","28-30"))

MMSEKM<-survfit(Surv(tt/365.25,cens)~mmsecat,data=data)

MMSEKMplot<-ggsurvplot(MMSEKM,ylab="Survival probability of institutionalisation",xlab="Survival years",data,legend="top",surv.median.line = "hv",legend.labs=c("MMSE:<24","MMSE:24-27","MMSE:28-30"))


data%>%
  group_by(mmsecat)%>%
  count()



aloneKM<-survfit(Surv(tt/365.25,cens)~livesalone,data=data)

aloneKMplot<-ggsurvplot(aloneKM,ylab="Survival probability of institutionalisation",xlab="Survival years",data,legend="top",surv.median.line = "hv",legend.labs=c("live with other","live alone"))


sexKM<-survfit(Surv(tt/365.25,cens)~sex,data=data)

sexKMplot<-ggsurvplot(sexKM,ylab="Survival probability of institutionalisation",xlab="Survival years",data,legend="top",surv.median.line = "hv",legend.labs=c("male","female"))


(aloneKMplot$plot | sexKMplot$plot) / MMSEKMplot$plot


```

```{r eval=FALSE}

#densityplot2, fig.height=5, fig.width=10, fig.align = "center",fig.cap = "\\label{ } Density plot of non-zero observed (blue) and the m=10 densities per variable calculated from the imputed data (thin red lines) of packyears.", fig.pos ='H'

imp.packyears<-pmm[["imp"]][["packyears"]]


packyearsnozero<-subset(data2,packyears>0)


 plot(density(packyearsnozero$packyears),col="darkblue",main=" ", xlab = "packyears",xlim=c(-100,200),ylim=c(0.000,0.025))
for (i in 1:10) {
  lines(density(imp.packyears[,i] ),col="deeppink3")
}
 
#In this study, the `r nrow(packyearsnozero)` patients with missing “packyears” variable are all smokers, which means pack years should be larger than zero. Therefore, fig \@ref(fig:densityplot2) shows the distribution for those with non-zero "packyears". We can see that the distribution between observed and imputed data is different.

#The discrepancies may be caused by a bad imputation model, by a missing data mechanism that is not MCAR or by a combination of both. To further compare the distributions of observed and imputed data of "packyears", we use the diagnostic tool proposed by @Diagnostic2016. The idea is that under MAR the conditional distributions should be similar if the assumed model for creating multiple imputations has a good fit. 

```


```{r eval=FALSE}
#diagnostic, fig.align = "center",fig.cap = "\\label{ } Packyears against missingness probability for observed and imputed values.", fig.pos ='H'


fit<-with(pmm,glm(ici(pmm)~agebl+sex+packyears+eversmok+livesalone+charlsonbl+updrsblpart3+hybl+sebl+mmsebltotal+mmseyr1total+cens+tt,family = binomial))

# agebl+agesymptomonset+sex+packyears+eversmok+livesalone+charlsonbl+updrsblpart3+hybl+sebl+mmsebltotal+mmseyr1total+cens+tt

ps<-rep(rowMeans(sapply(fit$analyses,fitted.values)),pmm$m +1)

xyplot(pmm, packyears~ps | as.factor(.imp),
       xlab="Probability that record is incomplete",
       ylab="Packyears",
       pch=c(1,19),
       col=mdc(1:2))


#The fig \@ref(fig:diagnostic) shows that the distributions of the blue and red points are quite similar, as expected under MAR. Therefore, the imputation model has a good fit.

```

```{r nomogram, eval=FALSE}



surv <- Survival(modelc)
surv5 <- function(x) surv(5*365,lp=x)
surv8 <- function(x) surv(8*365,lp=x)


plot(nomogram(modelc, 
              fun=list(surv5, surv8), 
              funlabel=c('5-year survival', '8-year survival')))

```
